hook: Read this one on a full screen and take your time, because the formatting is part of the experience. It presents itself as a classified file that has to check whether you are fit to read it, and that framing becomes the story. It deals with loss in a dark way, but its power is psychological rather than graphic.
whyItMatters: It is a standout among the wiki's meta-styled cognitohazard articles, where the document behaves as though it is reacting to the person reading it. It carries the class-of-76 tag, linking it to a small group of related works. The combination of an interactive format and quiet grief is a big part of why it stays with readers.
thingsToNotice:
The repeated phrase works like a mantra the file needs you to accept, and each repetition makes it sound less like a fact and more like an instruction. Watch the small intrusions: footnotes that contradict the main text, automated edits, a speaker label that changes partway through an interview.

Once verification fails, the article stops being a report and becomes a direct appeal, forcing you to choose which voice to trust. That ambiguity is the core: is the second voice a survivor telling the truth, or the anomaly reaching for one more person?
